verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The last snow melts from the roof tiles one drop at a time.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left the porch light burning all night —
a moth still circles it in daylight, confused.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A kettle forgets it's empty,
whistles anyway —
someone laughs in the next room.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I forgot my mother's face for a second today,
then the kettle answered it back to me.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Wind turns the calendar page early —
March arrives before we're ready,
smelling of someone else's garden.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I sweep yesterday's petals off the step —
the broom finds a coin instead,
heads up, warm from someone's pocket.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
I flip the coin toward the gutter stream —
it doesn't sink, just spins,
teaching the water a new way to shine.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A neighbor calls out from her window,
asking if I've seen her cat —
I say no, and mean it kindly.
